pairs: Dicebat autem et ad discipulos suos:
And he also said to his disciples:
and he had a steward of his estate.
et hic diffamatus est apud illum quasi dissipasset bona ipsius.
And this man was accused to him of having dissipated his goods.
‘What is this that I hear about you?
Give an account of your stewardship.
For you can no longer be my steward.’
And the steward said within himself:
quia dominus meus aufert a me villicationem?
For my lord is taking the stewardship away from me.
I am not strong enough to dig.
I am too ashamed to beg.
I know what I will do so that,
when I have been removed from the stewardship,
they may receive me into their houses.’
Convocatis itaque singulis debitoribus domini sui,
And so, calling together each one of his lord’s debtors,
‘How much do you owe my lord?’
‘In truth, how much do you owe?’
He said to him, ‘Take your record books,
And the lord praised the iniquitous steward,
in that he had acted prudently.
quia filii hujus sæculi prudentiores filiis lucis in generatione sua sunt.
For the sons of this age are more prudent with their generation than are the sons of light.
And so I say to you,
facite vobis amicos de mammona iniquitatis:
make friends for yourself using iniquitous mammon,
when you will have passed away,
they may receive you into the eternal tabernacles.
Whoever is faithful in what is least,
is also faithful in what is greater.
et qui in modico iniquus est,
And whoever is unjust in what is small,
is also unjust in what is greater.
Si ergo in iniquo mammona fideles non fuistis quod verum est,
So then, if you have not been faithful with iniquitous mammon,
who will trust you with what is true?
Et si in alieno fideles non fuistis, quod vestrum est,
And if you have not been faithful with what belongs to another,
who will give you what is yours?
Nemo servus potest duobus dominis servire:
No servant is able to serve two lords.
aut enim unum odiet, et alterum diliget:
For either he will hate the one and love the other,
aut uni adhærebit, et alterum contemnet.
or he will cling to the one and despise the other.
Non potestis Deo servire et mammonæ.
You cannot serve God and mammon.”
But the Pharisees, who were greedy,
qui erant avari: et deridebant illum.
were listening to all these things. And they ridiculed him.
Vos estis qui justificatis vos coram hominibus:
“You are the ones who justify yourselves in the sight of men.
quia quod hominibus altum est, abominatio est ante Deum.
For what is lifted up by men is an abomination in the sight of God.

quam de lege unum apicem cadere.
than for one dot of the law to fall away.
